note: CRTH2/DP2 antagonists (OC000459, AMG 853, AZD1981, fevipiprant) reached phase 3 on human-cell pharmacology and mouse allergy models; fevipiprant hit its eosinophil biomarker but missed exacerbations.
label: Asthma (CRTH2)

engagement.model: Human eosinophils and Th2 cells in vitro
engagement.note: Ramatroban abolished PGD2-driven migration of human eosinophils via CRTH2; this cell assay profiled every later antagonist in the class.
engagement.short: Antagonist blocks PGD2 eosinophil migration in vitro
engagement.quote: PGD2-stimulated human eosinophil migration was shown to be mediated exclusively through activation of CRTH2, and surprisingly, these effects were completely inhibited by ramatroban.
engagement.judgement: Opens the strip with the first orally available CRTH2 antagonist shown to block PGD2 chemotaxis of human eosinophils; OC000459, AZD1981 and fevipiprant were all later profiled in the same shape-change/chemotaxis assays (Pettipher 2012, Schmidt 2013, Sykes 2016).

engagement.model: Human eosinophils and Th2 cells in vitro
engagement.note: OC000459 cut post-allergen sputum eosinophils and ex-vivo PGD2 eosinophil shape change in 16 asthmatics; fevipiprant later cut sputum eosinophils 3.5-fold (Gonem 2016).
engagement.quote: Sputum eosinophil counts at 1 day post-allergen challenge were lower after OC000459 treatment (p=0.002).
engagement.confidence: medium (abstract only; n=16 crossover, shape-change n=7)
engagement.reason: Patient eosinophils fell as cells predicted
engagement.judgement: First published patient-side match (epub 2012, print 2013); ex-vivo PGD2 shape-change inhibition was only -33.6% (n=7) versus near-complete inhibition in vitro, so magnitude is direction_only. Fevipiprant (Gonem 2016, https://doi.org/10.1016/S2213-2600(16)30179-5) later reduced sputum eosinophils 3.5-fold vs placebo (p=0.0014) in 61 eosinophilic asthmatics, confirming but not changing the status. Barnes 2012 sputum-eosinophil fall was not significant vs placebo, so not used.

dose.model: Human whole-blood eosinophil shape change (ex-vivo PD)
dose.note: Whole-blood PGD2 shape-change potency (OC000459 pKB 7.5) anchored class PK/PD; fevipiprant doses were later set by clinical FEV1 dose-ranging, not occupancy.
dose.quote: OC000459 competitively antagonized eosinophil shape change responses induced by PGD2 in both isolated human leukocytes (pKB = 7.9) and human whole blood (pKB = 7.5) but did not inhibit responses to eotaxin, 5-oxo-eicosatetraenoic acid, or complement component C5a.
dose.judgement: Sykes 2016 (https://doi.org/10.1124/mol.115.101832) predicted fevipiprant's slow off-rate (t1/2 14.4 min) would give receptor coverage against pathological PGD2; Bateman 2017 (https://doi.org/10.1183/13993003.00670-2017) then picked 150 mg/day by FEV1 dose-ranging in patients (1-450 mg), and phase 3 ran 150 and 450 mg with 450 mg trending better (Brightling 2021). Wang 2021 (https://doi.org/10.1055/a-1381-6579) is a population-PK paper only (title verified via Europe PMC; abstract blocked by publisher). Singh 2013 ex-vivo shape-change inhibition at 200 mg bid was -33.6% (n=7), too thin to score as a dose miss. No source puts predicted occupancy beside patient response, so untested.

efficacy.note: Selective tool antagonist TM30089 reduced peribronchial eosinophilia and mucus-cell hyperplasia in OVA mice; clinical-stage compounds mostly skipped this model.
efficacy.short: Tool antagonist clears eosinophils in OVA mice
efficacy.quote: Furthermore, TM30089 and ramatroban, the latter used as a reference herein, similarly inhibited asthma pathology in vivo by reducing peribronchial eosinophilia and mucus cell hyperplasia.
efficacy.judgement: First in-vivo efficacy of a selective small-molecule CRTH2 antagonist in a mouse asthma model (ramatroban, a dual TP/CRTH2 drug, was the reference). The clinical compounds were largely characterised in agonist-challenge rat/guinea-pig eosinophilia models instead (Pettipher 2012; Schmidt 2013 reports AZD1981 could not be evaluated in mouse, rat or rabbit cells because they did not respond to DP2 agonists), so the mouse disease model is a class proxy.

efficacy.note: OC000459 improved per-protocol FEV1, quality of life and night symptoms in steroid-free moderate asthma; the full-analysis FEV1 primary endpoint missed.
efficacy.quote: In the FA population, the mean change in FEV1 was 7.1% on OC000459 compared with 4.3% on placebo (not significant); in the PP population, the mean changes were 9.2% and 1.8%, respectively (P=0.037).
efficacy.confidence: low (abstract only; primary endpoint missed in full-analysis set)
efficacy.judgement: Scored same because QoL (P=0.0113), night symptoms (P=0.008) and per-protocol FEV1 matched the mouse direction in a 132-patient 28-day trial, but the full-analysis FEV1 primary endpoint was not significant; a stricter re-scorer could hold this cell untested until 2013. Epub 2011-07-15, print January 2012.

efficacy.note: AMG 853 added to inhaled steroid moved neither ACQ nor FEV1 at any dose; fevipiprant later failed phase 3 despite clearing sputum eosinophils.
efficacy.quote: AMG 853 as an add-on to inhaled corticosteroid therapy demonstrated no associated risks but was not effective at improving asthma symptoms or lung function in patients with inadequately controlled moderate-to-severe asthma.
efficacy.confidence: medium (abstract only; dual DP1/DP2 antagonist, no engagement biomarker reported)
efficacy.reason: Mouse benefit; patients did not respond
efficacy.judgement: Contra dated to the first published in-class failure (vidupiprant/AMG 853, 396 patients, 12 weeks; epub 2012-11-20, print February 2013). Caveats: AMG 853 is a dual DP1/CRTH2 antagonist and the abstract reports no target-engagement biomarker, so a re-scorer could date contra to 2021 instead, when fevipiprant LUSTER-1/2 (Brightling 2021, https://doi.org/10.1016/S2213-2600(20)30412-4; 1,771 severe asthmatics, 52 weeks) showed no significant exacerbation reduction after multiplicity adjustment despite proven sputum-eosinophil engagement (Gonem 2016). Mouse-model relevance was itself doubtful: Schmidt 2013 (https://doi.org/10.1111/bph.12053) could not test AZD1981 in mouse, rat or rabbit cells because they did not respond to DP2 agonists.

safety.model: In-vitro off-target selectivity panels; animal toxicology unpublished
safety.note: OC000459 was clean on 69 receptors and 19 enzymes; no animal toxicology or regulatory review is public, and no model-patient safety comparison was found.
safety.short: Clean selectivity panel; tox never public
safety.quote: OC000459 had no significant inhibitory activity on a battery of 69 receptors and 19 enzymes including cyclooxygenase 1 (COX1) and COX2.
safety.judgement: Patient-side safety was placebo-like across the class: Busse 2013 'demonstrated no associated risks'; LUSTER-1/2 serious adverse events 9% in every arm; SPIRIT (Maspero 2021, https://doi.org/10.1186/s12931-021-01904-8; 2,538 patients, up to 104 weeks) 'safety profile similar to placebo'. The models' silence therefore held, but no CRTH2 antagonist was ever filed, so no FDA/EMA review names the toxicology package, and no primary source puts animal safety beside patient adverse events; left untested rather than same. A re-scorer accepting juxtaposition could set same at 2013 (Busse) or 2021 (Maspero).
